Subject: Re: SLA metric definitions, measurement method & escalation path

Nikhil — thanks for the draft. Our legal team has circulated a few targeted asks around how uptime is measured and how credits are calculated. Summary of their points (see attached PDF for clause markup):

- Measurement window: Acme requests a rolling 30-day availability calculation rather than calendar-month to reflect usage spikes.
- Exclusions: maintenance windows should be limited to a monthly 4-hour maintenance window per region; any additional planned downtime needs 7 days' notice and cannot be used to accrue credits.
- Credit formula: propose credits tied to minutes of unavailability during the measurement window (simple linear schedule). Current draft uses percentage-based buckets — legal prefers explicit minute bands and a cap per month.
- Proof/evidence: Acme requires exportable audit logs (request IDs + timestamps) and a monthly availability report delivered to Acme SREs.
- Escalation path: when availability falls below the threshold for two consecutive days, they want an on-call bridge including Redwood engineering, Acme SRE, and the AE.

Can you confirm which of these we can accept as written versus which require RL/ops internal sign-off? We want to avoid open-ended maintenance carve-outs.

Thanks — Steve

Attachments: OrderForm_ACME_v3_redline.pdf

Nikhil — reviewed Steve's asks and the attached redline. My read and suggested positions below. I have annotated the draft Order Form (see SLA_Metrics_Appendix_draft.docx) with strike/add comments. High level: we can accept most items with guarded language and operational limits.

1) Rolling 30-day measurement: acceptable if we keep a clause that final availability is calculated from Redwood's monitoring system and that Redwood's time-series is the single source of truth. Proposed sentence: "Availability shall be calculated on a rolling 30-day basis as measured by Redwood's monitoring tooling; Customer may request a report as set forth in Section X." This prevents parallel claims from Acme using their own tooling.

2) Maintenance windows: propose to counter with a monthly 6-hour maintenance window per region (not 4), but add a clause requiring Redwood to provide at least 48 hours' notice for any scheduled maintenance that may impact availability. We should not agree to a 7-day minimum for non-critical maintenance; that would cause operational friction.

3) Credit formula: we will not agree to uncapped per-minute liability. Counter-proposal: minute-band credits capped at X% of monthly fees (we should keep the cap as a negotiable figure but recommend 25% for mid-market). Suggest explicit band table in appendix; I'll draft the wording.

4) Evidence and logs: we can provide exportable event logs and a monthly availability report. Add data retention and redaction language: logs provided for SLA evidence will be redacted for other customers' data and provided in CSV format with request IDs and timestamps. Also include a clause that forensic-level log exports (full request traces) are subject to a data access request and may incur a nominal fee.

5) Escalation bridge: acceptable with scope. Recommend: automated alert + escalation to AE and SRE up to 48 hours after threshold breach; after 48 hours require an engineering bridge. We should not commit to on-call intervention for transient anomalies.

Next steps: I will produce a marked counterparty appendix by EOD tomorrow and flag the Order Form for commercial cap numbers. Lauren, can you advise on cap guidance (25% vs 15%)? Ops (will need ops to confirm rolling 30-day exports are feasible) — I will cc Ops once we have a draft.

Regards,
Kim
